it is because things draw it out.
The beginning is close to emotion,
the end is close to righteousness.
Those who understand emotion can bring it forth,
those who understand righteousness can take it in.
What is made good or not good—
In all cases, nature is the master,
but without striking, they do not ring.
if the mind does not draw it out, it does not emerge.

But for humans, learning may cause it.
All things are without exception different.
Within the four seas, their nature is one.
What is seen is called things;
what pleases one is called pleasure;
the arrangement of things is called circumstance;
what is done deliberately is called deliberate action.

The sages compared their categories and discussed their connections,
embodied their righteousness and regulated their patterns,
ordered their emotions and brought them in and out,
then again used them for teaching.
Teaching is what generates virtue within.
Facing affairs, it is formulated according to the situation;
its sequence follows the appropriate way.
it is used to achieve moderation.

Its dwelling in moderation is enduring;

The music of Zhèng and Wèi—
is not what one should listen to and follow.
All ancient music elevates the heart;
The Lài and Wǔ music takes;
the Sháo and Xià music expresses emotion.
Therefore, their hearts are not far.
Whenever there is sorrowful thought, grief follows;
whenever there is joyful thought, delight follows.
Of all mental activities, thinking is the most intense.
All human emotions can bring joy.
If one acts according to genuine emotion,
if not according to genuine emotion,
this is one who possesses beautiful emotions.
To have constancy among the people without teaching—
this is one whose nature is good.
To have the people encouraged without reward—
this is one who contains blessings.
To have the people in awe without punishment—
this is one who possesses a heart of awe.
To be humble yet honored by the people—
this is one who possesses virtue.
To be poor yet gathered around by the people—
this is one who possesses the Way.
this is one who has inner motivation.
To be disliked yet not blameworthy—
this is one who comprehends righteousness.
To be criticized yet not detestable—
this is one who is steadfast in benevolence.
this is one who knows the Way.
To hear the Way and turn upward—
this is one who associates with superiors.
To hear the Way and turn downward—
this is one who associates with inferiors.
To hear the Way and turn inward—
this is one who cultivates the self.
Associating with superiors is close to serving the ruler;
associating with inferiors and gaining the multitude is close to governing;
cultivating the self is close to attaining perfect benevolence.
To associate with those of the same direction—
this is based on the Way.
To associate with those of different directions—
To associate with those of shared joy—
To associate with those of different joys—
Governance within the family should aim for ease.
In general, the body should desire stillness and not agitation;
the heart should desire virtue and not falsity;
thoughts should desire depth and not divergence;
retreat should desire solemnity and not frivolity;
advance should desire compliance and propriety;
speech should desire directness and not drift;
dwelling should desire ease and freedom, not laxity.
The noble person, holding to his will, must have a firm and steadfast heart;
in speech, he must have sincere and honest trustworthiness;
in the rites of receiving guests, he must have a dignified and orderly demeanor;
in the rites of sacrifice, he must have a reverent and solemn respect;
in mourning, he must have a profound and continuous grief.
In general, when pleasing others, do not be stingy;
and when speaking of it, clearly exemplify it without falsity.
In all associations, do not be extreme;
When on the road, do not ponder;
do not speak alone or dwell alone;

only love from nature is close to benevolence.
There are five kinds of knowledge;
only the way of righteousness is close to loyalty.
